sentences.text: Parvodus is an extinct genus of hybodont sharks that lived during the Mesozoic era.
This animal belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes all cartilaginous fish.
It is classified within the parent group Lonchidiidae.
The genus was named by Rees and Underwood in 2001.
Scientists have recorded 81 fossil occurrences of this shark in the Paleobiology Database.
A species named P. ominechonensis was described by Breeden et al. in 2024 from Carnian deposits in Japan.
Another species, P. graciliani, was described by Ribeiro and França in 2026 from Tithonian deposits in Brazil.
The species P. graciliani is known from isolated teeth found in lacustrine deposits of the Aliança Formation in the Jatobá Basin.
The type species of the genus Parvodus is Lissodus rugianus.
This type species was originally described by Ansorge in 1990.
It is debated whether the species P. heterodon belongs in the genus Parvodus or should be placed in the genus Polyacrodus.
Similarly, it is debated whether the species "Hybodus" parvidens belongs in the genus Parvodus or should be assigned to the genus Polyacrodus.
